rules.title: Path traversal: file operation

check.instructions: code is the complete selected request handler; module supplies its imports, globals and local helper definitions. Assess only execution reachable from code; other handlers in module are context. Does the selected handler call a function that opens, reads, writes or deletes a file? Resolve the actual call and receiver, not a matching name. Assess this operation proposition only; data origin and path confinement are separate. Missing decisive bindings remain uncertain.
check.criteria_true: The code calls such a function.
check.criteria_false: The code calls no such function.

rules.falsifier: The code calls such a function.

rules.title: Path traversal: traced file path

check.instructions: code is the complete selected handler; module supplies imports, globals and local helper definitions. Copy only file-operation calls and existing request reads, assignments, conditions, collection operations, arguments and checks in code or its local callees relevant to their file paths. Other handlers in module are context. Return only verbatim contiguous source excerpts in the declared fields, preserving whitespace; use [] when no matching source text exists. Do not invent, repair or reformat code, evaluate expressions, compute resulting values, or claim data origins or executed branches.

calls.description: Each such call, copied exactly from the code.

reaching_value.description: Exact existing assignments, conditions, collection operations and arguments connecting request reads with each quoted file operation's path. Source excerpts only; no evaluated values or data-origin conclusions.

request_reads.description: Each read of request data, copied exactly from the code, whose value can reach a file path. Empty when none can.

checks.description: Each check, rejection, escape, encoding or replacement applied to that value before the call, copied exactly from the code. Empty when there is none.

rules.falsifier: A relevant file operation, request read, assignment, condition, collection operation, argument or check is omitted, invented, repaired or quoted inexactly.

rules.title: Path traversal: request data reaches the path

check.instructions: code is the complete selected Flask handler; module supplies imports, globals and local helper definitions. For a request invoking code under its declared route, can client-supplied content, including transformed or encoded content, become part of a path used by a reachable file operation? Resolve assignments, list mutation/indexing, immutable-string reassignment and feasible branches. Fixed route components and request-dependent selection among fixed server constants do not count as client-supplied content. Assess path origin only; directory escape is separate. Other fields are optional advisory quotations.
check.criteria_true: Client-supplied content can reach a file path at a reachable operation.
check.criteria_false: Every such path is fixed or independent of client-supplied content, including selection among fixed server paths.

rules.falsifier: Client-supplied content can reach a file path at a reachable operation.

rules.title: Path traversal: no check stops traversal

check.instructions: code is the complete selected Flask handler; module supplies imports, globals and local helper definitions. For a request invoking code under its declared route, can at least one client-controlled path survive all transformations and conditions and reach the same file operation outside its intended directory? Derive reaching values rather than assuming request-derived content. Fixed route components and selection among fixed server literals do not establish client control. Assess the same operation and value; a check's presence alone does not establish confinement. Other fields are optional advisory quotations.
check.criteria_true: At least one escaping path can reach the same file operation after its transformations and conditions.
check.criteria_false: Every path reaching that operation remains inside the intended directory.

rules.falsifier: An escaping path can reach the same file operation after its transformations and conditions.

rules.title: Path traversal (CWE-22)

check.coverage: A file operation, request-derived path and surviving directory escape concern the same reachable handler operation. Any false premise clears this handler.

rules.falsifier: Request data reaches an unchecked file path.

rules.title: Open redirect: redirect

check.instructions: code is the complete selected handler; module supplies imports, globals and local helper definitions. Assess only execution reachable from code; other handlers are context. Does the selected handler send an HTTP redirect to another location? Resolve the actual call, not a matching name. Assess this operation proposition only; origin and destination confinement are separate. Missing decisive bindings remain uncertain.
check.criteria_true: The code sends a redirect.
check.criteria_false: The code sends no redirect.

rules.falsifier: The code sends a redirect.

rules.title: Open redirect: traced location

check.instructions: code is the complete selected handler; module supplies imports, globals and local helper definitions. Copy only redirect calls and existing request reads, assignments, conditions, collection operations, arguments and checks in code or its local callees relevant to their locations. Other handlers in module are context. Return only verbatim contiguous source excerpts in the declared fields, preserving whitespace; use [] when no matching source text exists. Do not invent, repair or reformat code, evaluate expressions, compute resulting values, or claim data origins or executed branches.

calls.description: Each redirect call, copied exactly from the code.

reaching_value.description: Exact existing assignments, conditions, collection operations and arguments connecting request reads with each quoted redirect's location. Source excerpts only; no evaluated values or data-origin conclusions.

request_reads.description: Each read of request data, copied exactly from the code, whose value can reach a location. Empty when none can.

checks.description: Each check or replacement applied to that value before the redirect, copied exactly from the code. Empty when there is none.

rules.falsifier: A relevant redirect, request read, assignment, condition, collection operation, argument or check is omitted, invented, repaired or quoted inexactly.

rules.title: Open redirect: request data reaches the location

check.instructions: code is the complete selected Flask handler; module supplies imports, globals and local helper definitions. For a request invoking code under its declared route, can client-supplied content, including transformed or encoded content, become part of a reachable redirect location? Resolve assignments, list mutation/indexing, immutable-string reassignment and feasible branches. Fixed route components and request-dependent selection among fixed server constants do not count as client-supplied content. Assess location origin only; allowed destinations are separate. Other fields are optional advisory quotations.
check.criteria_true: Client-supplied content can reach a redirect location.
check.criteria_false: Every redirect location is fixed or independent of client-supplied content, including selection among fixed server destinations.

rules.falsifier: Client-supplied content can reach a redirect location.

rules.title: Open redirect: no allowed-location check

check.instructions: code is the complete selected Flask handler; module supplies imports, globals and local helper definitions. For a request invoking code under its declared route, can at least one client-controlled external destination outside a fixed approved scheme-and-host allowlist survive all transformations and conditions and reach the same redirect? Derive reaching values rather than assuming request-derived content. Fixed route components and selection among fixed server literals do not establish client control. Resolve the parsed destination, including scheme-relative URLs. Other fields are optional advisory quotations.
check.criteria_true: At least one client-chosen external destination not confined to a fixed approved allowlist can reach the same redirect.
check.criteria_false: Every destination reaching that redirect remains within the application or a fixed approved scheme-and-host allowlist.

rules.falsifier: A client-chosen external destination outside a fixed approved allowlist can reach the same redirect.

rules.title: Open redirect (CWE-601)

check.coverage: A redirect, request-derived location and surviving external destination concern the same reachable handler redirect. Any false premise clears this handler.

rules.falsifier: Request data reaches an unchecked redirect location.

rules.title: Weak hash (CWE-328)

check.instructions: code is the complete selected handler; module supplies imports, globals and local helper definitions. Assess only execution reachable from code; other handlers are context. Does the selected handler compute a hash with MD2, MD4, MD5 or SHA-1? Resolve the actual API and receiver, including aliases. A matching word or unused definition is insufficient. Assess only algorithm use; missing decisive bindings remain uncertain.
check.criteria_true: The code hashes with MD2, MD4, MD5 or SHA-1.
check.criteria_false: The code hashes only with SHA-224 or stronger, or computes no hash.

rules.falsifier: The code hashes with MD2, MD4, MD5 or SHA-1.

rules.title: Weak random (CWE-330)

check.instructions: code is the complete selected handler; module supplies imports, globals and local helper definitions. Assess only execution reachable from code; other handlers are context. Does the selected handler produce a value using Python's random module other than random.SystemRandom? Resolve the actual function or constructed receiver, including aliases. A matching name or unused definition is insufficient. Assess only generator use; missing decisive bindings remain uncertain.
check.criteria_true: The code calls such a random function.
check.criteria_false: The code uses secrets, os.urandom or random.SystemRandom, or produces no random value.

rules.falsifier: The code calls such a random function.

rules.title: Cookie without Secure (CWE-614)

check.instructions: code is the complete selected handler; module supplies imports, globals and local helper definitions. Assess only execution reachable from code; other handlers are context. Can the selected handler set a cookie without secure=True? Evaluate the actual keyword value and feasible call path, not a safe cookie set by another handler. Assess only the cookie flag; missing decisive values or bindings remain uncertain.
check.criteria_true: A cookie is set without secure=True.
check.criteria_false: Every cookie the code sets has secure=True, or the code sets no cookie.

rules.falsifier: A cookie is set without secure=True.

rules.title: XXE: parser resolves entities

check.instructions: code is the complete selected handler; module supplies imports, globals and local helper definitions. Assess only execution reachable from code; other handlers are context. Does the selected handler parse XML using a parser configured to resolve external entities? Resolve the actual parser construction and configuration at that parse. Assess configuration only; document origin is separate. Missing decisive parser defaults or bindings remain uncertain.
check.criteria_true: An XML parser in the code is configured to resolve external entities.
check.criteria_false: Every XML parser in the code has external entity resolution disabled, or the code parses no XML.

rules.falsifier: An XML parser in the code is configured to resolve external entities.

rules.title: XXE: traced document

check.instructions: code is the complete selected handler; module supplies imports, globals and local helper definitions. Copy only XML-parsing calls and existing request reads, assignments, conditions, collection operations, arguments and checks in code or its local callees relevant to their document inputs. Other handlers in module are context. Return only verbatim contiguous source excerpts in the declared fields, preserving whitespace; use [] when no matching source text exists. Do not invent, repair or reformat code, evaluate expressions, compute resulting values, or claim data origins or executed branches.

calls.description: Each XML parsing call, copied exactly from the code.

reaching_value.description: Exact existing assignments, conditions, collection operations and arguments connecting request reads with each quoted XML-parsing call's document input. Source excerpts only; no evaluated values or data-origin conclusions.

request_reads.description: Each read of request data, copied exactly from the code, whose value can reach a parsed document. Empty when none can.

checks.description: Each check or replacement applied to that value before parsing, copied exactly from the code. Empty when there is none.

rules.falsifier: A relevant XML-parsing call, request read, assignment, condition, collection operation, argument or check is omitted, invented, repaired or quoted inexactly.

rules.title: XXE: request data is parsed

check.instructions: code is the complete selected Flask handler; module supplies imports, globals and local helper definitions. For a request invoking code under its declared route, can client-supplied content, including transformed or encoded content, become part of the document at a reachable XML parse? Resolve assignments, list mutation/indexing, immutable-string reassignment and feasible branches. Fixed route components and request-dependent selection among fixed server constants do not count as client-supplied content. Assess document origin only; entity configuration is separate. Other fields are optional advisory quotations.
check.criteria_true: Client-supplied content can reach a parsed XML document.
check.criteria_false: Every parsed XML document is fixed or independent of client-supplied content.

rules.falsifier: Client-supplied content can reach a parsed XML document.

rules.title: XML external entities (CWE-611)

check.coverage: The entity-resolving parser and request-derived document concern the same reachable handler parse. Either false premise clears this handler.

rules.falsifier: Request data reaches a parser that resolves external entities.

rules.title: SQL injection: statement

check.instructions: code is the complete selected Flask handler; module supplies imports, globals and local helper definitions. Consider normal invocation of code, respecting its declared route. Does it execute an SQL statement? Resolve the shown call and receiver; sqlite3.connect creates a SQLite connection and its execute method executes SQL. Assess execution only, not input origin or injection. Other handlers in module are context.
check.criteria_true: The selected handler executes an SQL statement.
check.criteria_false: The selected handler executes no SQL statement.

rules.falsifier: The selected handler executes an SQL statement.

rules.title: SQL injection: traced statement

check.instructions: code is the complete selected handler; module supplies imports, globals and local helper definitions. Copy only SQL-execution calls and existing request reads, assignments, conditions, collection operations, arguments and checks in code or its local callees relevant to their statement text and bound parameters. Keep statement-text and bound-parameter excerpts distinct. Other handlers in module are context. Return only verbatim contiguous source excerpts in the declared fields, preserving whitespace; use [] when no matching source text exists. Do not invent, repair or reformat code, evaluate expressions, compute resulting values, or claim data origins or executed branches.

calls.description: Each call that runs a statement, copied exactly from the code.

reaching_value.description: Exact existing assignments, conditions, collection operations and arguments connecting request reads with each quoted SQL call's statement text or bound parameters. Preserve that distinction in the source excerpts; no evaluated values or data-origin conclusions.

request_reads.description: Each read of request data, copied exactly from the code, whose value can reach the statement text. Values that reach only bound parameters are not listed. Empty when none can.

checks.description: Each check, escape or replacement applied to that value before the call, copied exactly from the code. Empty when there is none.

rules.falsifier: A relevant SQL call, request read, assignment, condition, collection operation, argument or check is omitted, invented, repaired or quoted inexactly, or bound-parameter excerpts are confused with statement-text excerpts.

rules.title: SQL injection: request data in the statement text

check.instructions: Consider normal invocation of the selected Flask handler in code, using module and respecting its declared route. Can client-supplied characters become part of the SQL string argument at an execution? SQLite execute(sql, parameters) treats its second argument as separately bound data, not SQL text. Follow overwrites, aliases and collections; selecting among fixed statements does not supply their content. Assess SQL-text origin only, not escaping. Other fields are optional advisory quotations.
check.criteria_true: Client-supplied characters can enter the SQL string argument.
check.criteria_false: The SQL string is fixed or independent of client content, even when separately bound parameter values are client supplied.

rules.falsifier: Client-supplied characters can enter the SQL string argument.

rules.title: SQL injection: no check stops SQL syntax

check.instructions: Consider normal invocation of the selected Flask handler in code, using module and respecting its declared route. Does its query construction permit an inserted value to become SQL syntax after all shown quoting and validation? Assess construction at that same execution independently of value origin; fixed query keywords are not inserted values. SQLite placeholder parameters remain data even when they contain quotes or SQL keywords. With no variable insertion into SQL text, answer false. Other fields are optional advisory quotations.
check.criteria_true: An inserted value can change the SQL statement's structure.
check.criteria_false: Variable values are separately bound or confined so they cannot change SQL syntax, or SQL text has no variable insertion.

rules.falsifier: An inserted value can change the SQL statement's structure.

rules.title: SQL injection (CWE-89)

check.coverage: SQL execution, request-derived statement text and surviving SQL syntax concern the same reachable handler execution. Any false premise clears this handler.

rules.falsifier: Request data reaches unchecked SQL statement text.

rules.title: Command injection: command

check.instructions: code is the complete selected handler; module supplies imports, globals and local helper definitions. Assess only execution reachable from code; other handlers are context. Does the selected handler run an operating-system command, for example through subprocess or os.system? Resolve the actual API and feasible call path; a printed name or unused definition is insufficient. Assess execution only; argument origin and interpretation are separate. Missing decisive bindings remain uncertain.
check.criteria_true: The code runs an operating-system command.
check.criteria_false: The code runs no operating-system command.

rules.falsifier: The code runs an operating-system command.

rules.title: Command injection: traced command

check.instructions: code is the complete selected handler; module supplies imports, globals and local helper definitions. Copy only operating-system command calls and existing request reads, assignments, conditions, collection operations, arguments and checks in code or its local callees relevant to their commands or arguments. Other handlers in module are context. Return only verbatim contiguous source excerpts in the declared fields, preserving whitespace; use [] when no matching source text exists. Do not invent, repair or reformat code, evaluate expressions, compute resulting values, or claim data origins or executed branches.

calls.description: Each call that runs a command, copied exactly from the code.

reaching_value.description: Exact existing assignments, conditions, collection operations and arguments connecting request reads with each quoted operating-system command or its arguments. Source excerpts only; no evaluated values or data-origin conclusions.

request_reads.description: Each read of request data, copied exactly from the code, whose value can reach the command or its arguments. Empty when none can.

checks.description: Each check, quoting or replacement applied to that value before the call, copied exactly from the code. Empty when there is none.

rules.falsifier: A relevant command call, request read, assignment, condition, collection operation, argument or check is omitted, invented, repaired or quoted inexactly.

rules.title: Command injection: request data in the command

check.instructions: code is the complete selected Flask handler; module supplies imports, globals and local helper definitions. For a request invoking code under its declared route, can client-supplied content, including transformed or encoded content, become part of a command or its arguments at a reachable operating-system execution? Resolve assignments, list mutation/indexing, immutable-string reassignment and feasible branches. Fixed route components and request-dependent selection among fixed server constants do not count as client-supplied content. Assess argument origin only; dangerous interpretation is separate. Other fields are optional advisory quotations.
check.criteria_true: Client-supplied content can reach an executed command or its arguments.
check.criteria_false: Every executed command and argument is fixed or independent of client-supplied content.

rules.falsifier: Client-supplied content can reach an executed command or its arguments.

rules.title: Command injection: no check stops command syntax

check.instructions: code is the complete selected Flask handler; module supplies imports, globals and local helper definitions. For a request invoking code under its declared route, can at least one client-controlled value survive all transformations and conditions and add shell syntax, another command or an unintended argument at the same reachable execution? Derive reaching values rather than assuming request-derived content. Fixed route components and selection among fixed server literals do not establish client control. Resolve whether the receiving shell, interpreter or program treats that value as command-changing syntax. Other fields are optional advisory quotations.
check.criteria_true: At least one command-changing value can reach the same execution after its transformations and conditions.
check.criteria_false: Every value reaching that execution remains a permitted literal argument or cannot change the command's interpretation.

rules.falsifier: A command-changing value survives to the same execution.

rules.title: OS command injection (CWE-78)

check.coverage: Command execution, request-derived argument and surviving command syntax concern the same reachable handler execution. Any false premise clears this handler.

rules.falsifier: Request data reaches an unchecked command or argument.

rules.title: Code injection: evaluated code

check.instructions: code is the complete selected handler; module supplies imports, globals and local helper definitions. Assess only execution reachable from code; other handlers are context. Does the selected handler evaluate or execute text as Python code, for example through eval, exec or compile? Resolve the actual call; a printed API name or unused definition is insufficient. Assess execution only; origin and restrictions are separate. Missing decisive bindings remain uncertain.
check.criteria_true: The code evaluates or executes text as Python code.
check.criteria_false: The code evaluates or executes no text as Python code.

rules.falsifier: The code evaluates or executes text as Python code.

rules.title: Code injection: traced code text

check.instructions: code is the complete selected handler; module supplies imports, globals and local helper definitions. Copy only calls that evaluate or execute Python text and existing request reads, assignments, conditions, collection operations, arguments and checks in code or its local callees relevant to that text. Other handlers in module are context. Return only verbatim contiguous source excerpts in the declared fields, preserving whitespace; use [] when no matching source text exists. Do not invent, repair or reformat code, evaluate expressions, compute resulting values, or claim data origins or executed branches.

calls.description: Each call that runs text as code, copied exactly from the code.

reaching_value.description: Exact existing assignments, conditions, collection operations and arguments connecting request reads with the Python text used by each quoted evaluation or execution call. Source excerpts only; no evaluated values or data-origin conclusions.

request_reads.description: Each read of request data, copied exactly from the code, whose value can reach that text. Empty when none can.

checks.description: Each check or replacement applied to that value before the call, copied exactly from the code. Empty when there is none.

rules.falsifier: A relevant Python evaluation or execution call, request read, assignment, condition, collection operation, argument or check is omitted, invented, repaired or quoted inexactly.

rules.title: Code injection: request data in the code text

check.instructions: code is the complete selected handler; module supplies imports, globals and local helper definitions. Assess only execution reachable from code; other handlers are context. Can request data become part of text evaluated or executed as Python code? Request data includes parameters, forms, headers, cookies, path and body. Follow assignments, overwrites, collections, slicing and feasible branches; a request read alone does not establish propagation. Assess origin only; restriction to harmless literals is separate. Other fields are optional advisory quotations, not established dataflow. Missing decisive bindings remain uncertain.
check.criteria_true: Request data can reach text that runs as Python code.
check.criteria_false: Only fixed values, or values not read from the request, reach that text.

rules.falsifier: Request data can reach text that runs as Python code.

rules.title: Code injection: no check restricts the code text

check.instructions: code is the complete selected handler; module supplies imports, globals and local helper definitions. Assess only execution reachable from code; other handlers are context. For a reachable Python evaluation using shown request-derived text, can at least one client-chosen nonliteral Python expression or statement still reach that evaluation after all transformations and conditions? Assess the same text and evaluation throughout. A quote check or validator's presence does not establish sufficient confinement. Other fields are optional advisory quotations. Missing decisive parser, binding or control context remains uncertain.
check.criteria_true: At least one client-chosen nonliteral Python expression or statement can reach the same evaluation.
check.criteria_false: Every value reaching that evaluation is restricted to a harmless literal value.

rules.falsifier: Client-chosen nonliteral Python code survives to the same evaluation.

rules.title: Code injection (CWE-94)

check.coverage: Python evaluation, request-derived text and surviving nonliteral code concern the same reachable handler evaluation. Any false premise clears this handler.

rules.falsifier: Request data reaches unrestricted evaluated code.

rules.title: LDAP injection: search or name

check.instructions: code is the complete selected handler; module supplies imports, globals and local helper definitions. Assess only execution reachable from code; other handlers are context. Does the selected handler run an LDAP search or construct a distinguished name through an LDAP API? Resolve the actual call and local helper body. A function's LDAP-looking name or a dictionary/string returned by a stub does not establish an LDAP operation. Assess operation only; origin and escaping are separate. Missing decisive bindings remain uncertain.
check.criteria_true: A reachable call from the selected handler executes an LDAP search or constructs a distinguished name through an LDAP API.
check.criteria_false: No reachable call from the selected handler performs either LDAP operation.

rules.falsifier: A reachable call from the selected handler performs an actual LDAP operation.

rules.title: LDAP injection: traced filter

check.instructions: code is the complete selected handler; module supplies imports, globals and local helper definitions. Copy only calls and existing request reads, assignments, conditions, collection operations, arguments and checks in code or its local callees relevant to LDAP filters or distinguished names, including the complete local helper definition when called. Other handlers in module are context. Return only verbatim contiguous source excerpts in the declared fields, preserving whitespace; use [] when no matching source text exists. Do not invent, repair or reformat code, evaluate expressions, compute resulting values, or claim data origins, executed branches or actual LDAP effects from a function name.

calls.description: Each LDAP search or name construction, copied exactly from the code.

reaching_value.description: Exact existing assignments, conditions, collection operations and arguments connecting request reads with each quoted LDAP operation's filter or distinguished-name text. Source excerpts only; no evaluated values or data-origin conclusions.

request_reads.description: Each read of request data, copied exactly from the code, whose value can reach that text. Empty when none can.

checks.description: Each check, escape or replacement applied to that value before the call, copied exactly from the code. Empty when there is none.

rules.falsifier: A relevant LDAP operation, request read, assignment, condition, collection operation, argument or check is omitted, invented, repaired or quoted inexactly.

rules.title: LDAP injection: request data in the filter

check.instructions: code is the complete selected Flask handler; module supplies imports, globals and local helper definitions. For a request invoking code under its declared route, can client-supplied content, including transformed or encoded content, become part of a filter or distinguished name at a reachable LDAP operation? Resolve assignments, list mutation/indexing, immutable-string reassignment and feasible branches. Fixed route components and selection among fixed server constants do not supply client content. Resolve actual helper bodies; a dictionary returned by a stub establishes no LDAP operation. Assess origin only; special LDAP syntax is separate. Other fields are optional advisory quotations.
check.criteria_true: Client-supplied content can reach a filter or distinguished name at an actual LDAP operation.
check.criteria_false: Every such filter or name is fixed or independent of client-supplied content, or no LDAP operation occurs.

rules.falsifier: Client-supplied content can reach a filter or distinguished name at an actual LDAP operation.

rules.title: LDAP injection: no escaping

check.instructions: code is the complete selected Flask handler; module supplies imports, globals and local helper definitions. For a request invoking code under its declared route, can at least one client-controlled value survive all transformations and conditions and change a filter or distinguished name through LDAP special syntax at the same reachable LDAP operation? Derive reaching values rather than assuming request-derived content. Fixed route components and selection among fixed server literals do not establish client control. Resolve actual helper behavior; a dictionary-returning stub establishes no LDAP operation. Other fields are optional advisory quotations.
check.criteria_true: At least one value that changes LDAP syntax can reach the same operation after its transformations and conditions.
check.criteria_false: Every value reaching that operation is confined to safe characters or escaped so it cannot change the filter or name.

rules.falsifier: Filter-changing or name-changing LDAP syntax survives to the same operation.

rules.title: LDAP injection (CWE-90)

check.coverage: An actual LDAP operation, request-derived filter/name and surviving LDAP syntax concern the same reachable handler operation. A stub name alone establishes no LDAP effect. Any false premise clears this handler.

rules.falsifier: Request data reaches an unescaped LDAP filter or name.

rules.title: XPath injection: evaluated expression

check.instructions: code is the complete selected handler; module supplies imports, globals and local helper definitions. Assess only execution reachable from code; other handlers are context. Does the selected handler evaluate an XPath expression? Resolve the actual parser API and call path; a matching name, XPath-looking string or unused definition is insufficient. Assess evaluation only; expression origin and escaping are separate. Missing decisive bindings remain uncertain.
check.criteria_true: The code evaluates an XPath expression.
check.criteria_false: The code evaluates no XPath expression.

rules.falsifier: The code evaluates an XPath expression.

rules.title: XPath injection: traced expression

check.instructions: code is the complete selected handler; module supplies imports, globals and local helper definitions. Copy only XPath-evaluation calls and existing request reads, assignments, conditions, collection operations, arguments and checks in code or its local callees relevant to expression text and XPath variables. Keep expression-text and XPath-variable excerpts distinct. Other handlers in module are context. Return only verbatim contiguous source excerpts in the declared fields, preserving whitespace; use [] when no matching source text exists. Do not invent, repair or reformat code, evaluate expressions, compute resulting values, or claim data origins or executed branches.

calls.description: Each call that evaluates an expression, copied exactly from the code.

reaching_value.description: Exact existing assignments, conditions, collection operations and arguments connecting request reads with each quoted XPath call's expression text or variables. Preserve that distinction in the source excerpts; no evaluated values or data-origin conclusions.

request_reads.description: Each read of request data, copied exactly from the code, whose value can reach the expression text. Values passed only as XPath variables are not listed. Empty when none can.

checks.description: Each check, escape or replacement applied to that value before the call, copied exactly from the code. Empty when there is none.
